stimulus_text: Schools must appoint a security lead.
Staff must lock classroom doors and move students to the safe corner.
If a lockdown is announced, occupants shall remain in place until released.
Evacuate using the nearest exit, except when the exit is blocked by smoke.
Follow the response options in Annex B when an intruder is reported.
Appropriate personnel should secure the perimeter.
Doors are to be locked from the inside during a lockdown.
Each centre shall maintain a written emergency response plan.
Provide a visual alert equivalent for occupants who cannot hear the siren.
Verify whether all occupants can reach the secure room within three minutes.
Conduct at least two lockdown drills each school year.
Revise the lockdown procedure using findings from the annual drill review.
Special education classrooms must have an assigned buddy for each evacuation route.
Settings should consider lockdown, invacuation, or evacuation as response options.
Plans should be inclusive and accessible for learners with special educational needs.
Personal emergency evacuation plans must be in place for identified individuals.
If safe, call emergency services and report your location.
Remain silent and still until an all-clear is given.
Keep hands visible and empty when officers enter the room.
The titular shall elaborate, implement, maintain, and review the self-protection plan.
Staff should report concerning behaviour to the threat-assessment team.
School violence is a serious societal concern requiring attention.
Exercises must proceed without surprise effects and without replica weapons.
If the school spans distant sites, each site shall prepare its own plan and two annual exercises.
On hearing the alarm, close and lock doors, then move to the safe area and await instructions.
Consider individual needs. Provide strobe alarms in hallways.
